page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-16GB is an x86_64 architecture virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes a bundled 150 GB local SSD and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The processor supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, along with cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, though it lacks AMX support.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and high single-threaded compression throughput, with gzip compression reaching 38.22 GB/sec. However, because the 2 vCPUs are shared, multi-core and multi-threaded workloads show significant degradation. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores all fall into the weak or bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only small block cached speeds at 423.32 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 68.14 GB/sec.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this server is less efficient for sustained parallel computing, software compilation, or database operations, which return poor to weak benchmark results. However, its generous 16.0 GB memory capacity relative to its 2 vCPUs offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive but CPU-bursty workloads. It is best suited for static web serving, single-threaded data processing, lightweight caching, and running small language model inference, where it maintains average performance.
